newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica confirms digital TV accord.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica confirms digital TV accord.

text.p: Spain's Telefonica said on Thursday that it had signed an agreement with domestic and international partners to create the first digital television platform in Spain, due to be operational in March 1997.
Telefonica estimates investing 29 billion pesetas over 10 years in the project.

The firm will develop a joint-venture in digital television by December 16 with state television network Radio Television Espanola, with Antena 3 and Mexico's Televisa as well as with regional stations Telemadrid, Canal 9, Television de Galicia and Television de Catalunya.
Telefonica de Espana will have a 35 percent stake in the new company, which has not been named as yet.
Partners have agreed that up to 30 percent of the share capital "could eventually be sold on the stock market," the statement said.

The platform will begin broadcasting on December 24 with 14 television channels. Once the pilot phase is completed, in March 1997 commercial broadcasting will begin with approximately 40 diferent channels, planned to rise to 70 eventually.
